items.title: About the journal
items.seoDescription: Why Studio Halden keeps a journal, and how to get in touch.

blocks.heading: Why a journal
blocks.html:
A building takes years, and most of what we learn on the way is forgotten by the next project. The journal is where we write it down: what worked, what did not, and what we would do differently.

Comments, corrections and questions are welcome: journal@halden.example.

items.title: What a model teaches that a drawing cannot
items.author: ingrid@studio-halden.test
items.seoDescription: A week with a 1:50 model of the forest house changed three decisions about the roof.

blocks.headline: What a model teaches that a drawing cannot

image.alt: A white architectural model on a studio table

blocks.html:
For the forest house we had drawn the roof a dozen times, and it looked right every time. Then we built it at 1:50 and held it up to a window: the overhang shaded the wrong side of the courtyard.

Three decisions changed that week. The drawing had been correct; it had simply been silent about light. A model is never silent.

items.title: Concrete in the rain
items.author: jonas@studio-halden.test
items.seoDescription: Why we keep a wet-weather photo diary of every concrete wall we build.

image.alt: A courtyard with pale concrete walls after rain

blocks.html:
Every wall we pour gets a photo diary: the day it is stripped, after its first winter, after its fifth. Rain is the honest test. A good wall darkens evenly and dries into the same colour; a poor one stains in stripes.

The diaries are how we decide next year's mix.
